import html # Predefined HTML template for forum posts. # It contains three placeholders: # {title} – the title of the post # {body} – the main body content # {points} – an unordered list of discussion points FORUM_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
{points}
""" def build_post_html(topic_title: str, body_text: str, list_items: list[str]) -> str: """ Create a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- topic_title : str The title or main topic of the forum post. body_text : str The main body content of the forum post. list_items : list[str] A collection of user‑provided discussion points or options in markdown format. Returns ------- str A string containing the fully formatted and sanitized HTML representation of the forum post, including the header, message body, and safely rendered discussion points. Raises ------ TypeError If any of the arguments is not of the expected type. """ # Input validation if not isinstance(topic_title, str): raise TypeError("topic_title must be a string") if not isinstance(body_text, str): raise TypeError("body_text must be a string") if not isinstance(list_items, list) or not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in list_items): raise TypeError("list_items must be a list of strings") # Sanitize user input to prevent XSS safe_title = html.escape(topic_title, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body_text, quote=True) # Render the list items as an unordered list. # Each item is escaped; markdown formatting is not parsed to avoid # unintended HTML injection. For simplicity we keep the raw text. if list_items: safe_points = "
    \n" + "\n".join(f"
  • {html.escape(item, quote=True)}
    • " for item in list_items) + "\n
" else: safe_points = "" # Format the final HTML using the template html_output = FORUM_POST_FORMAT.format( title=safe_title, body=safe_body, points=safe_points ) return html_output.strip()
